correctness.rationale: Fixing the existential witnesses yields at most \(2^{\binom{k}{2}}\) one-vertex profiles. A profile class above the stated size has a monochromatic triangle in the \(2^k\)-colored pair graph, and those three vertices have identical atomic types over the witnesses for every assignment using at most three outside vertices. Cloning that 3-type therefore preserves the universal matrix and yields all larger orders. Conversely, a triangle-free \(2^k\)-coloring of \(K_{R_{2^k}(3)-1}\) can be encoded independently in every one-vertex profile class, and a single quantifier-free implication forces the exact upper bound. Equality/repetition cases are controlled by irreflexivity. A fresh exhaustive replay independently confirmed every red/blue coloring of \(K_6\) has a monochromatic triangle and the endpoint values \(N_3(0)=2,N_3(1)=6\).

final_claim: For simple 3-uniform hypergraphs and sentences with \(k\) leading existentials followed by exactly three universals, every finite spectrum has maximum at most \(N_3(k)=k+(R_{2^k}(3)-1)2^{\binom{k}{2}}\), and this bound is attained for every \(k\); any model above it implies models of every order at least \(k+3\).
